blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models introduce language reasoning into end-to-end autonomous driving. They output a language decision together with a trajectory, which makes the planner more interpretable. However, in existing methods the language decision is either an independent output or an index that selects among similar candidate trajectories, and its annotations are not verified against the trajectory. As a result, the language decision and the trajectory are often inconsistent in closed-loop driving. To address this, we propose Commit2Drive, a framework that imposes the language decision as a consistency constraint on trajectory planning. The decision is a commitment, a maneuver class with a continuous parameter that one deterministic rule reads from any trajectory, and it is grounded in facts reported by the perception of the model itself. A Maneuver Bank maps the commitment to a code with a kinematic meaning, and consistency losses train the planner to execute every admissible decision of a scene, so that the trajectory follows the decision. An automatic data pipeline supplies the supervision. Decisions are labeled from the future motion of the expert, counterfactual executions train the decision and the trajectory together, and rule-based functions with a Vision-Language Model (VLM) generate, review and refine the language annotations. The code is a lookup that involves no hidden state of the language model, so Commit2Drive is extensible to rule-based decisions, which the same planner executes without retraining. Commit2Drive uses a 0.5B language model and runs closed-loop inference online on a single consumer graphics card. On Bench2Drive, Commit2Drive reaches a Driving Score (DS) of 78.50 and a Success Rate (SR) of 55.91% with a lightweight model, which is competitive with the state of the art, and greatly reduces the language-action inconsistency. Code will be released soon.
blocks.zh: Vision-Language-Action(VLA)模式将语言推理引入到端到端自主驱动中. 它们输出一个语言决定和一个轨迹,这使得规划者更容易被解释. 然而,在现有方法中,语言决定要么是独立的产出,要么是在类似的候选轨迹中选择的索引,其注释没有与轨迹相对照加以核实。 因此,在闭路驾驶中,语言决定和轨迹往往不一致. 为了解决这个问题,我们提议采用Committee2Drive这一框架,将语言决定作为轨道规划的一致性限制。 决定是一种承诺,一种具有连续参数的操作类,一个决定性规则从任何轨迹读取,并以模型本身感知所报告的事实为基础。 一个Maneuver银行描绘了对一个具有动能意义的代码的承诺,一致性损失训练规划者执行一个场景的每一个可受理的决定,以便轨迹遵循决定. 自动数据管道提供监督。 根据专家未来的动议,决定被贴上标签,反事实处决将决定和轨迹结合在一起,基于规则的功能具有视觉语言模型(VLM)生成、审查和完善语言说明。 代码是一种搜索,不涉及语言模型的隐藏状态,因此Cont2Drive可以被扩展到基于规则的决定,同一位规划者在没有再培训的情况下执行. Co通2Drive使用0.5B语言模型,并在单一消费图形卡上在线运行闭路推论. 在Bench2Drive上,Committee2Drive的驾驶分数(DS)为78.50分,成功率(SR)为55.91%,采用轻量级模式,与最先进的水平竞争,并大大降低了语言动作不一致. 代码很快就会发布

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Autonomous driving requires a model to understand complex traffic scenes and to plan safe trajectories.
Traditional End-to-End (E2E) methods [ 3 , 15 , 24 , 23 ] integrate perception, prediction and planning into one differentiable network and map sensor inputs directly to trajectories.
These methods have made great progress, but they work as black boxes and give no explanation for the trajectory they output.
With the rapid progress of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in visual understanding and reasoning, recent work extends them to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for driving [ 46 , 18 , 9 , 39 , 64 , 10 ] .
A VLA model outputs chain-of-thought reasoning or a language decision together with the trajectory.
This paradigm improves generalization with the world knowledge of the VLM, and it lets human drivers understand the decisions of the model.
blocks.zh:
自主驾驶需要一种模型来理解复杂的交通场景并规划安全的出行轨迹.
传统的端到端(E2E)方法[3, 15, 24, 23]将感知,预测和规划整合到一个不同的网络和地图传感器输入直接到轨迹.
这些方法取得了很大进展,但它们作为黑匣子发挥作用,没有解释它们输出的轨迹.
随着Visual-Langage Models(VLMs)在视觉理解和推理方面的快速进步,近期的作品将其扩展至Visual-Langage-Action(VLA)模型用于驾驶[46,18,9,39,64,10].
VLA模型输出-思维链推理或语言决定与轨迹.
这个范式随着世界对VLM的了解而改进了通俗化,它让人类的驱动力能够理解模型的决定.

blocks.en:
Most current VLA models produce the two outputs in parallel ( c).
OmniDrive [ 48 ] lets the language head output both the language decision and the trajectory as text [ 35 , 55 , 46 , 18 ] .
Text tokens are discrete and carry no notion of numerical distance, so waypoints generated token by token are not precise enough [ 9 ] .
ORION [ 9 ] improves on this design and predicts the waypoints with a separate numerical planner [ 39 , 32 , 50 ] .
Combined with Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training on the trajectory [ 32 , 10 ] , this design alleviates the above problem to some extent.
However, neither design constrains the two outputs, which are often inconsistent [ 37 , 34 , 59 ] .
On Bench2Drive [ 22 ] , the decision stated by MindDrive contradicts its own planned trajectory on the vast majority of the frames ( a and Tab. 2 ).
This is because the language annotations of the training data are not checked against the expert trajectory, and no explicit constraint links the decision to the trajectory.
The trajectory is usually the more accurate of the two ( Sec. 4.2 ), because subsequent training, including RL post-training, mainly rewards the trajectory and neglects the language decision.
As a result, the language decision becomes redundant, and the interpretability that the VLA paradigm promises is greatly limited.
Recent methods such as MindDrive [ 10 ] and DriveMA [ 62 ] attempt to solve this problem, but they align the two outputs only in form and do not effectively constrain their consistency.
The decision token of MindDrive selects among candidate trajectories that fall into the same maneuver class on most frames, so it is an index without a meaning ( b).
DriveMA considers the future motion of the expert only in the labels of the language decision and does not resolve the contradictions inside the chain-of-thought reasoning.
A data pipeline that enforces the consistency of the whole annotation is still missing.
blocks.zh:
目前大多数的VLA模式同时产生两种产出(c)。
OmniDrive [48] 让语言头输出语言决定和轨迹作为文本 [35, 55, 46, 18].
文本符号是离散的,没有数字距离的概念,因此由符号生成的路由符号不够精确 [9].
Orion [9] 改进了这一设计,并用单独的数值计数器预测了路由点[39,32,50].
这种设计与轨道[32,10]上的强化学习(RL)后训练相结合,在一定程度上缓解了上述问题.
然而,这两种设计都不限制两种产出,两者往往不一致[37、34、59]。
在Bench2Drive [22]上,MindDrive所陈述的决定与它自己在绝大多数框架(a和Tab. 2)上规划的轨迹相矛盾。
这是因为培训数据的语言说明没有与专家的轨迹相对照,也没有将决定与轨迹挂钩的明确限制。
轨迹通常对两者更为准确(sec.4.2.),因为后续的训练,包括RL后训练,主要奖励轨迹而忽略了语言决定.
因此,语言决定变得多余,而VLA范式承诺的可解释性也非常有限.
MindDrive [10] 和 DriveMA [62]等近期方法试图解决这个问题,但它们只以形式对齐两种产出,并没有有效地限制其一致性.
MindDrive的决定符号在大多数帧上属于同一类的候选轨迹中选择,因此它是一个没有意义(b)的索引.
DriveMA只在语言决定的标签中考虑专家未来的动议,并没有解决思维链推理中的矛盾.
仍缺少一个数据管道,可加强整个注释的一致性。

blocks.en:
To address this challenge, we propose Commit2Drive, a VLA framework that imposes the language decision as a consistency constraint on trajectory planning ( c).
Specifically, the language decision is stated as a commitment , which consists of a maneuver class, such as slow down, and a target value, such as the speed to reach.
Facts reported by the perception of the model rule out the decisions that the scene does not allow.
A Maneuver Bank then maps the commitment to a code with a kinematic meaning, and the planner generates the trajectory conditioned on this code.
To make the planner follow the decision, we design consistency losses that supervise every admissible decision of a scene, with the expert trajectory for the decision of the expert and a counterfactual execution for each alternative.
To provide the supervision, we build an automatic data pipeline in which rule-based functions and a VLM generate, review and refine the language annotations.
In addition, the mapping takes only a decision as input, so the framework is extensible to mature rule-based decision modules, which can be plugged in without modification.
Extensive experiments on the closed-loop Bench2Drive benchmark show that Commit2Drive, with a lightweight 0.5B language model, is competitive with the state of the art, reaching a Driving Score (DS) of 78.50 and a Success Rate (SR) of 55.91%, and reduces the inconsistency between the language decision and the planned trajectory to 1.8%.
blocks.zh:
为了应对这一挑战,我们提议采用一个VLA框架Committee2Drive,将语言决定作为轨道规划的一致性限制(c)。
具体地说,语言决定被说成是一种承诺,它包括一个动作类,如减速,以及目标值,如达到的速度.
模型感知报告的事实排除了现场不允许的决定.
一个曼纽佛 Bank随后绘制了对具有动态含义的代码的承诺图,计划者生成以这个代码为条件的轨迹.
为了让规划者遵循决定,我们设计了一致性损失,以监督一个场景的每一个可受理的决定,以及专家决定的轨迹和每个选择的反事实处决。
为了提供监督,我们建立了一个自动数据管道,其中基于规则的功能和一个VLM生成、审查和完善语言说明。
此外,映射仅作为输入做出一个决定,因此框架可以被扩展到成熟的以规则为基础的决策模块,可以不作修改地插入.
对闭路客座2Drive基准的广泛实验表明,Cont2Drive具有轻量级0.5B语言模型,与最先进的水平具有竞争力,达到78.50%的驱动分数和55.91%的成功率,并将语言决定和计划轨迹之间的不一致降低到1.8%.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We propose Commit2Drive, a language-constrained planning framework for VLA autonomous driving models. By introducing a Maneuver Bank and consistency losses, Commit2Drive turns the language decision from a mode index into a semantic constraint that the trajectory is trained to satisfy, substantially improving the consistency between language decisions and planned trajectories. • We introduce an automatic data pipeline that combines rule-based functions with a VLM to generate, review and refine language annotations, reducing their reasoning contradictions. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first to ground counterfactual reasoning in the facts of visual perception and to train the language decision and the trajectory on it together, so that the two outputs of the model stay consistent. • Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of Commit2Drive, achieving 78.50 DS and 55.91% SR on the Bench2Drive benchmark with a lightweight 0.5B language model. The lookup of the Maneuver Bank also decouples the language decision from the hidden states of the language model, which makes the framework extensible to rule-based decisions.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: We review E2E driving and language-action consistency.
blocks.zh: 我们审查E2E驾驶和语言行动的一致性。

blocks.en: 2.1 End-to-End Autonomous Driving
blocks.zh: 2.1 端到端自动驾驶

blocks.en:
E2E autonomous driving learns perception, prediction and planning in one differentiable network that maps sensor inputs to trajectories [ 3 , 51 , 13 , 15 , 24 ] .
UniAD [ 15 ] and VAD [ 24 ] unify several tasks on bird’s-eye-view representations, and GenAD [ 61 ] and DiffAD [ 49 ] model planning as a generative problem.
However, these models lack the reasoning ability and common sense that complex scenarios require, so recent methods build driving models on VLMs [ 43 , 63 , 30 , 33 ] .
DriveGPT4 [ 55 ] , EMMA [ 18 ] and OmniDrive [ 48 ] output control signals or trajectories as text.
Senna [ 25 ] and DriveVLM [ 46 ] pair a VLM with a separate planner, and ORION [ 9 ] links the VLM to a generative planner with a planning token.
AutoVLA [ 64 ] , ReCogDrive [ 32 ] and AlphaDrive [ 26 ] are further optimized with RL.
MindDrive [ 10 ] uses a Decision Expert and an Action Expert that share one language model, and optimizes its language decisions with trajectory-level rewards in online RL.
blocks.zh:
E2E自主驾驶在一个不同的网络中学习感知,预测和规划,该网络将传感器输入到轨迹[3,51,13,15,24].
UniAD [15] and VAD [24] 统一了鸟眼-观赏表现的几个任务,GENAD [61] and DiffAD [49] 模型规划作为一个基因问题.
然而,这些模型缺乏复杂情景所需要的推理能力和常识,因此最近的方法在VLMs上建立了驱动模型[43,63,30,33].
DriveGPT4 [55],EMMA [18]和OmniDrive [48] 输出控制信号或轨迹作为文本.
Senna [25] and DriveVLM [46] 配对一副VLM并配有单独的规划器,而ORION [9] 将VLM与有规划符的基因规划器联系起来.
AutoVLA [64],ReCogDrive [32] 和 AlphaDrive [26] 与 RL 进一步优化.
MindDrive [10] 使用决策专家与行动专家共享一种语言模式,并优化其语言决策,在在线RL中以轨迹级别奖励.

blocks.en: 2.2 Language-Action Consistency
blocks.zh: 2.2 语言行动一致性

blocks.en:
The explanation of a model need not reflect the computation behind its prediction [ 19 , 47 , 29 ] .
In driving, prior works align textual explanations or reasoning with the predicted actions [ 28 , 27 , 17 ] .
SimLingo [ 39 ] trains the planner on simulated alternative futures to follow language instructions.
Alpamayo-R1 [ 50 ] rewards the consistency between reasoning and action in RL post-training, and CF-VLA [ 38 ] revises its meta-actions by counterfactual reflection.
DriveMA [ 62 ] labels meta-actions from the future motion of the expert, generates the meta-action before the trajectory and rewards their agreement.
Audits find the reasoning of driving VLMs and VLA models often ungrounded or weakly coupled to the trajectory [ 53 , 37 , 34 ] , and run-time monitors flag or reject such mismatches [ 59 , 52 ] .
These methods measure or encourage consistency through data, losses and rewards, while guaranteed constraints rely mainly on rule-based executors and shields outside VLA planners [ 5 , 40 , 1 , 41 , 14 ] .
blocks.zh:
对一个模型的解释不需要反映其预测背后的计算 [19, 47, 29].
在驾驶时,前作将文字解释或推理与所预测的行动相配合[28,27,17].
SimLingo [39] 训练计划员模拟替代期货遵循语言指令.
Alpamayo-R1[50]奖励了RL后训练中的推理与行动的一致性,而CF-VLA[38]则通过反事实反思来修改其元动作.
DriveMA [62] 从专家的未来运动中标出元动作,在轨迹前生成元动作并奖励他们的同意.
审计发现驱动VLMs和VLA模型的推理往往没有根据,或与轨迹相弱结合[53,37,34],运行时显示器标出或拒绝这种错配[59,52].
这些方法通过数据、损失和奖励衡量或鼓励一致性,而有保障的限制主要依靠在《维也纳条约法公约》规划者之外以规则为基础的执行者和盾牌[5、40、1、41、14]。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
In this section, we present Commit2Drive in detail.
As illustrated in Fig. 2 , following MindDrive [ 10 ] , Commit2Drive comprises a Decision Expert and an Action Expert, which share one VLM and differ only in their Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) [ 12 ] parameters.
The Decision Expert serves as the language decision head and states the driving decision, while the Action Expert serves as the trajectory execution head and generates the trajectory.
We first formulate trajectory planning under a language consistency constraint ( Sec. 3.1 ).
We then introduce the consistent language-action mapping, which maps the language decision to a code with a kinematic meaning through a Maneuver Bank and trains the Action Expert with consistency losses to follow it ( Sec. 3.2 ).
Next, the counterfactual decision-action data pipeline pairs every admissible decision of a scene with a trajectory, and reviews and refines the language annotations ( Sec. 3.3 ).
Finally, the mapping makes Commit2Drive extensible to rule-based decisions, which drive the same Action Expert ( Sec. 3.4 ).

blocks.en:
To satisfy Eq. 3 , the language decision and the action must be consistent, and the language decision must constrain the action directly.
This requires the language decision to carry semantics that the action can follow.
However, in existing methods the decision reaches the action only as an index, which carries no semantics.
We therefore introduce a Maneuver Bank, which gives the language decision a kinematic meaning and maps it to the action, and consistency losses, which train the Action Expert to follow it.

blocks.en: 3.3 Counterfactual Decision-Action Data Pipeline
blocks.zh: 3.3 反事实决定-行动数据管道

blocks.en: Figure 3 : Counterfactual decision-action data pipeline. From a raw log frame, rule-based functions generate the decision label, the counterfactual executions, the admissible set and the perception facts. A VLM and human experts review them; flagged records are fixed at the rule and regenerated, or refined .
blocks.zh: 图3:反事实决策行动数据管道。 从原始的日志框架中,基于规则的函数生成决定标签,反事实处决,可接受集和感知事实. 核查组和人类专家审查这些记录;标记的记录固定在规则上并重新生成或改进。

blocks.en:
The mapping above needs supervision that existing datasets do not provide.
Their language annotations are not clearly tied to the action. A decision label often does not describe what the expert does next, and the reasoning text can contradict the scene or itself.
Moreover, counterfactual data has not yet been used to train the language decision and the action together.
To fill this gap, we build a counterfactual decision-action data pipeline.
As shown in Fig. 3 , rule-based functions generate the records of every frame, and a VLM reviews and refines the language annotations.
The pipeline runs automatically on the raw logs of Bench2Drive [ 22 ] .

上述绘图需要现有数据集不提供的监督。
他们的语言说明与动作没有明显的联系. 一个决定标签往往不描述专家接下来做什么,推理文本可以与场景或自身相矛盾.
此外,反事实数据尚未用于培训语言决定和共同行动。
为了填补这一空白,我们建立了一个反事实决策行动数据管道。
如图3所示,基于规则的函数生成每个帧的记录,并有VLM审查并完善了语言说明.
管道在Bench2Drive的生木上自动运行 [22].

blocks.en:
With one decision and one trajectory per scene, a model can produce both from the scene alone, without the trajectory following the decision.
We therefore pair every admissible decision of a scene with a trajectory, and rule-based functions write four records for every frame.
(i) Decision label : the commitment ( d ¯ , θ ¯ ) (\bar{d},\bar{\theta}) is read from the next 3 s of the expert trajectory and rendered as the decision sentence, so the label and the trajectory agree by construction.
(ii) Counterfactual executions : for every other decision k k , the path of the expert is re-timed with a speed profile of decision k k , which gives a trajectory a ¯ k \bar{a}_{k} with Φ ⁡ ( a ¯ k ) = k \Phi(\bar{a}_{k})=k .
It is rolled out against the logged motion of the other agents on an occupancy grid [ 13 ] and marked infeasible if it collides.
(iii) Admissible set : 𝒟 F \mathcal{D}_{F} keeps the decisions whose execution is feasible and that no traffic rule forbids. keep and accel are forbidden when the stop line of a red light or of a stop sign is within reach.
(iv) Perception facts : the fact sentences, rendered from the logged scene by the templates that are used at inference.
With these records, the admissible set tells the Decision Expert which decisions are admissible, and the counterfactual executions tell the Action Expert what each of them looks like ( Eq. 5 ).

blocks.en:
A language annotation is a short chain of reasoning, and its contradictions are also learned by the model.
A VLM [ 2 ] therefore takes two roles.
As a blind reviewer, it judges whether a decision sentence contradicts the scene, whether a fact sentence invents or omits an object, and whether an alternative decision is safe and legal.
As an editor, it revises reasoning text that contradicts itself.
Errors that originate in a rule or a template are corrected at their source, and the records are regenerated and reviewed again.
Finally, human experts check a random sample of the records.
The resulting dataset covers the base set of Bench2Drive (Sec. C of the supplementary material).
blocks.zh:
一种语言注释是一种短的推理链,它的矛盾也由模型来学习.
因此,VLM[2]具有两个作用。
作为盲目审查者,它判断裁判判决是否与场景相矛盾,事实判决是发明还是省略对象,另类判决是否安全合法.
作为编辑,它修改了自相矛盾的推理文本.
起源于规则或模板的出错会在源头被纠正,再生成并审查记录.
最后,人类专家检查记录的随机样本.
由此产生的数据集涵盖Bench2Drive(补充材料的C项)的基数集。

The Action Expert reads the decision only through the code of Eq. 4 , which involves no hidden state of the language model.

blocks.en:
We train and evaluate Commit2Drive on Bench2Drive [ 22 ] , a closed-loop benchmark for end-to-end autonomous driving based on the CARLA simulator [ 7 ] .
We adopt the official base set of 1000 clips, with 950 for training and 50 for open-loop validation.
The clips are annotated by our data pipeline ( Sec. 3.3 ), which yields 234,769 training and 12,806 validation frames.
Closed-loop evaluation uses the official 220 short routes across 44 interactive scenarios.

我们的数据管道(第3.3节)对剪辑作了说明,提供了234 769次培训和12 806个验证框架。

blocks.en:
All models are trained on 4 NVIDIA A100 graphics cards.
We employ the pretrained EVA-02-L [ 8 ] as the vision encoder and the lightweight Qwen2-0.5B [ 56 ] as the base Large Language Model (LLM).
Commit2Drive is trained in two stages, Imitation Learning (IL) and online RL, both following MindDrive [ 10 ] .
Only the Action Expert is initialized from the released checkpoint of MindDrive, which gives the trajectory generation a prior.
This Action Expert has been trained by IL alone, as the online RL of MindDrive updates only its Decision Expert and value network.
In the IL stage, the Decision Expert is fine-tuned with LoRA to state the decision, and the Maneuver Bank, the fusion MLP and the speed branch are then trained with ℒ cons \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cons}} , while all other modules are frozen.
Closed-loop evaluation runs online on a single RTX 4090, and every measured result is the median over multiple random seeds.

A traffic-light rule decides stop or slow at a red light that governs the ego lane, and a collision-avoidance rule decides stop when a hazard is within the time-to-collision threshold.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduce Commit2Drive, a VLA framework that imposes the language decision as a consistency constraint on trajectory planning.
A Maneuver Bank maps the language decision to a code with a kinematic meaning, and consistency losses train the Action Expert to follow it.
An automatic data pipeline, in which rule-based functions and a VLM generate, review and refine the annotations, supplies the supervision.
Extensive experiments on Bench2Drive demonstrate that Commit2Drive, with a lightweight 0.5B language model, is competitive with the state of the art and greatly reduces the inconsistency between the language decision and the planned trajectory.
The framework is also extensible to existing rule-based methods, whose decisions drive the same Action Expert without retraining.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们引入了Committee2Drive,这是一个VLA框架,将语言决定作为轨迹规划的一致性限制.
一个曼纽佛 Bank将语言决定映射到一个具有动态含义的代码,一致性损失训练了行动专家遵循.
自动数据管道,即基于规则的功能和VLM生成、审查和完善说明,提供监督。
对Bench2Drive的广泛实验表明,Cont2Drive具有轻量级的0.5B语言模型,具有与最先进水平的竞争力,并会大大地减少语言决定和计划轨迹之间的不一致.
该框架也适用于现有的有章可循的方法,这些方法的决定促使同一个行动专家没有再培训。

blocks.en:
This work addresses only the say-do gap inside the model, and its driving performance exceeds the baseline by a small margin.
The say-exec gap, which lies between the model and the physical execution of its plan, remains unsolved and is left to future work.
We hope that it brings new inspiration to the autonomous driving community on the consistency between language decisions and trajectories.

由模式与实际执行计划之间的言行执行差距仍未解决并留给未来工作。
我们希望它能给自主驱动社区带来新的灵感,使其了解语言决定与轨迹的一致性。

blocks.en: Q1. What are the differences between Commit2Drive and MindDrive?
blocks.zh: 问题1. Cont2Drive和MindDrive有什么区别?

blocks.en:
Commit2Drive adopts the architecture of MindDrive [ 10 ] , in which a Decision Expert and an Action Expert share one VLM, and initializes its Action Expert from the released MindDrive checkpoint ( Sec. D.2 ).
In MindDrive, the decision is a speed token that selects one of several candidate trajectories ( Eq. 2 ).
The token is an index, and no term requires the selected candidate to follow it.
The candidates of MindDrive are nearly identical on most frames, and its output follows a forced token on a minority of the frames ( Sec. E.4 ).
In Commit2Drive, the decision is a commitment ( d , θ ) (d,\theta) that the deterministic rule Φ \Phi reads from any trajectory.
The Maneuver Bank maps the commitment to a code with a kinematic meaning, and the consistency losses supervise every admissible decision of a scene with a trajectory that realizes it.
The decisions of a scene then yield distinct trajectories, and the trajectory follows a forced decision on nearly all frames ( Tab. A12 ).
The supervision also differs: the decision labels of Commit2Drive are read from the future motion of the expert, so the label and the trajectory agree by construction, and the records are reviewed ( Sec. C ).

blocks.en: Q2. Is the consistency between the decision and the trajectory guaranteed at inference?
blocks.zh: 问题2. 在推论中,决定与轨迹的一致性是否得到保证?

blocks.en:
It is learned and not guaranteed.
We relax the indicator of Eq. 3 into the consistency losses of Eq. 5 and apply no projection or rejection at inference.
We therefore measure the consistency in two ways: with the say-do gap in closed loop and in open loop ( Tab. 2 and Sec. E.2 ) and with interventions that force the decision to another value ( Sec. E.4 ).
In both, the trajectory departs from the decision on few frames.
Since Φ \Phi is a deterministic rule on the planned trajectory, a remaining violation can be detected at run time.
We do not use such a check in any reported result.

blocks.en: Q3. Why is conditioning the Action Expert on the decision not sufficient?
blocks.zh: 问题3. 为何对行动专家的决定作出限制是不够的?

blocks.en:
On expert data, every scene comes with one decision, and this decision is a function of the scene.
A planner can then reproduce the expert from its hidden state h a h_{a} alone, and the imitation loss does not constrain its output under any other decision.
We state this formally in Sec. D.3 .
This agrees with what we observe for MindDrive, whose output follows a forced speed token on a minority of the frames ( b).
The counterfactual executions add every admissible decision of a scene to the training data, each with its own target, so only the decision tells the targets apart.
Without them, the say-do gap rises ( Tab. 3 ), the trajectories of different decisions move closer together, and the trajectory follows a forced decision far less often ( Tab. A10 ).

在专家数据上,每个场景都有一个决定,这个决定是场景的一个功能.
计划人员然后可以独自复制专家的隐藏状态h a h_{a},而模仿损失并不限制其在任何其他决定下的输出.
我们正式在D. 3中陈述这一点。
这与我们对MindDrive的观察一致,MindDrive的输出遵循了少数帧(b)上的强制速度符.
反事实处决将一个场景的每一个可接受的决定都添加到训练数据中,每个场景都有自己的目标,所以只有决定将目标分开.
没有它们,言行差距会上升(Tab. 3),不同决定的轨迹会更加接近,而轨迹遵循强制决定的频率要低得多(Tab. A10.

blocks.en: Q4. How does the counterfactual data differ from the Action Dreaming of SimLingo?
blocks.zh: 问题4. 反事实数据与"SimLingo的动作梦"有何不同?

blocks.en:
SimLingo [ 39 ] simulates alternative futures to train the planner to follow external language instructions.
These futures are paired with instructions, and not with the decision that the model itself states in its commentary.
In our interventions on its released checkpoint, the trajectory follows an explicit instruction on nearly all frames, but it follows the commentary far less often when the commentary is forced to another decision ( Tab. A12 ).
In Commit2Drive, the counterfactual executions are paired with the decision of the model itself.
The same records supervise the Decision Expert, through the admissible set, and the Action Expert, through the counterfactual executions.
The admissible set is computed from the logged scene, so the alternatives are limited to the decisions that pass its collision check and its traffic rules ( Sec. C.1 ).
blocks.zh:
SimLingo [39]模拟另类期货 训练计划员遵循外语指令.
这些期货与指示相配,而不是模型本身在评注中所表述的决定.
在我们对其已放行的检查站的发言中,轨迹遵循关于几乎所有框架的明确指示,但当评注被迫作出另一项决定时(A12. Tab. A12.),则遵循评注的情况要少得多。
在CommitteeDrive中,反事实处决与模型本身的决定对应.
同样的记录通过可受理的一套程序监督决定专家,通过反事实处决监督行动专家。
可受理的套装是从被记录的场景中计算出来的,因此替代品仅限于通过碰撞检查的决定和交通规则(第C.1节)。

blocks.en: Q5. Why does the say-exec gap remain large when the say-do gap is small?
blocks.zh: 问题5. 当说行差距很小时,为什么说行差距仍然很大?

blocks.en:
The two gaps compare the stated decision with different trajectories: the say-do gap with the trajectory that is planned at the same step, which the consistency constraint covers, and the say-exec gap with the trajectory that the vehicle executes afterward.
Since the model re-plans at every step, the executed trajectory results from many consecutive plans, and a decision that is stated at one step can be replaced at the next.
The planned and the executed trajectory also differ for the baselines, as their do-exec gap shows ( Tab. A13 ).
Commit2Drive lowers the say-exec gap, but a large part of it remains ( Tab. 2 ).
This remainder concerns the consistency of the decisions of consecutive steps, which the per-step constraint of Eq. 3 does not cover, and we leave it to future work.

blocks.en: Q6. Why does the decision space contain only speed decisions?
blocks.zh: 问题6. 为什么决定空间只包含速度决定?

blocks.en:
The Action Expert has a path branch and a speed branch ( Fig. 2 ).
In the annotations of MindDrive [ 10 ] , the model on which Commit2Drive is built, the path token is the navigation command of Bench2Drive, so the decision that the model makes by itself is the speed decision.
The released checkpoint confirms this: its path token equals the navigation command on the validation frames, and its open-loop error comes almost entirely from the speed along the path ( Sec. D.1 ).
We therefore keep the path branch frozen and constrain the speed decision.
The formulation does not depend on this choice: any decision that a deterministic rule can read from a trajectory can be stated as a commitment.
We leave path decisions to future work.

blocks.en: Q7. What is the role of the VLM in the data pipeline?
blocks.zh: 问题7. VLM在数据管道中的作用是什么?

blocks.en:
The VLM does not produce the labels.
Rule-based functions generate all four records of a frame from the raw log. The decision label is read from the future motion of the expert, and the counterfactual executions, the admissible set and the perception facts are computed from the logged scene ( Sec. C.1 ).
The VLM [ 2 ] then acts in two roles, as a blind reviewer that judges the records without knowing their origin or the verdict of the rule-based functions, and as an editor that revises reasoning text.
When the reviewer disagrees because of an error that originates in a rule or a template, we correct it at its source and regenerate the records, so the correction applies to every frame.
In the example of Fig. 3 , the reviewer judges that keeping the current speed toward a red light is illegal, and the rule that builds the admissible set is corrected to forbid keep when the stop line is within reach ( Eq. A5 ). Fig. A5 shows a record of this kind before and after the correction.
blocks.zh:
VLM不生产标签.
基于规则的函数从原始日志中生成一个帧的全部四个记录. 裁决书的标签取自专家未来的动议,反事实处决、可受理的一组和认知事实取自记录的场景(第C.1节)。
VLM [2]随后扮演了两个角色,一个是盲目评论员,在不知道记录的来源或基于规则的功能判断的情况下判断记录,另一个是编辑员,负责修改推理文本.

blocks.en: C Details on the Counterfactual Decision-Action Data
blocks.zh: C 反事实决定-行动数据详情

blocks.en:
The language annotations on which MindDrive [ 10 ] is trained are not checked against the expert trajectory.
Their speed token agrees with the decision that the expert realizes over the next 3 s on 40.0% of the labeled frames (mapping of Sec. C.3 ).
To supply the supervision that the consistent language-action mapping needs, we build an automatic data pipeline on the raw logs of the Bench2Drive base set [ 22 ] , without new recordings.
This section details the pipeline ( Sec. C.1 ), the resulting dataset ( Sec. C.2 ) and the mapping that expresses the decisions of existing models in our decision space ( Sec. C.3 ).

为了提供一致的语言动作绘图需要的监督,我们在Bench2Drive基础集的原始日志上搭建自动数据管道[22],没有新的录音.
本节详细介绍管道(第C.1节)、生成的数据集(第C.2节)以及表达我们决策空间中现有模型决定的绘图(第C.3节)。

The contradictions of an annotation are also learned by the model, so the records are reviewed.
The reviewer is the 32B version of Qwen3-VL [ 2 ] with greedy decoding.
It receives the six camera images of a frame, a list of ground-truth facts from the simulator and the prompts of Tab. A2 , and it answers in JSON.
The review covers a sample of the validation records: the decision sentence and the fact sentences of 600 frames, 150 for each decision, and the admissibility of 300 pairs of a frame and a decision, of which 150 are admissible, 75 are forbidden at a red light and 75 are infeasible.
The review is blind: the items are shuffled and carry random identifiers, and the reviewer is told neither the origin of a sentence nor the verdict of the rule-based functions.
For the admissibility items, the future motion of the ego vehicle is withheld as well.
The reviewer reads the decision in plain words.
As a reference, the decision of the original annotation of each frame is rendered and reviewed in the same way.
The reviewer finds a contradiction between the decision sentence and the motion of the ego vehicle in 62.5% of the original annotations and in 26.7% of ours.
It agrees with the admissible set on 66.7% of the pairs: it rejects all 75 decisions that a red light forbids and 62.7% of the infeasible ones, and it accepts 52.0% of the admissible ones.

The resulting dataset covers the base set of Bench2Drive, with 950 clips and 234,769 frames for training and 50 clips and 12,806 frames for open-loop validation ( Tab. A3 ).
A label exists for 196,769 training frames and 10,806 validation frames.
Every labeled frame carries four records: the decision label, the counterfactual executions of the other decisions, the admissible set and the perception facts. stop is the most frequent decision, with 37.5% of the training labels, because the vehicle is at rest in many frames. accel follows with 29.1%, keep with 20.7% and slow with 12.7%.
For the training frames, 422,141 counterfactual executions are generated, of which 334,315 are admissible.
The labeled training frames have 2.67 admissible decisions on average, and 77.5% of them have at least two, so that the Action Expert sees most scenes under more than one decision.
A red light governs the ego lane on 18.3% of the labeled training frames, and a traffic rule forbids the decision of the expert on 2.4%. Fig. A1 shows the distribution of the decisions and of their target values.

The second stage follows the online RL of MindDrive [ 10 ] : rollouts are collected in CARLA [ 7 ] , and the Decision Expert is updated by proximal policy optimization (PPO) on the collected steps.

The reward is that of MindDrive, − 1 -1 for a penalty event, + 1 +1 for a completed route and 0 otherwise.

blocks.en:
Tab. A8 lists the evaluated models, and Tab. A9 extends Tab. 2 with SimLingo [ 39 ] , with the normalized gap of Eq. A11 and with the baselines on the routes of Dev10.
SimLingo is trained on its own dataset and states its decision as a commentary, so it is not listed in Tab. 2 .
Its say-exec gap of 21.0% is the lowest of the three baselines, while its commentary and its own plan still disagree on 49.3% of the frames for the speed decision and on 43.4% for the yield decision.
The normalized gaps show that the small yield gaps of MindDrive and ORION do not indicate agreement.
Their normalized gaps are 0.84 and 0.97, so their stated decision and their planned trajectory agree barely more often than two independent outputs.
In open loop, on the 10,806 labeled validation frames, the say-do gap of Commit2Drive is 0.4% and its normalized gap 0.006.

SimLingo接受自有数据集的培训,并将其决定作为评注来表述,因此不在Tab中列出. 2 (中文(简体) ).

blocks.en:
On the open-loop validation frames, the expert trajectory tells which of the two outputs is wrong.
The speed token of MindDrive matches the decision of the expert on 33% of the frames, and its planned trajectory on 71%.
For ORION, the yield decision of the language head matches the expert on 49% of the evaluated frames, and its planned trajectory on 80%.
For both models, the trajectory is the more accurate output, in line with Sec. 4.2 .
In closed loop, the most frequent conflict of MindDrive is a token that maintains the speed while the plan accelerates, on 15,360 of its 24,317 logged frames.
blocks.zh:
在开放的验证框架上,专家的轨迹显示两种输出中哪一种是错误的.
MindDrive的速率标志与专家关于33%的相匹配,其计划轨迹为71%.
对ORION来说,语言负责人的产量决定与专家在49%的评价框架上一致,其计划轨迹为80%。
对于两种模型来说,轨迹是更准确的输出,符合第4.2条.
在闭环中,MindDrive最常发生的冲突是一个在计划加速的同时保持速度的标志,在它的24,317个被登录的帧中的15,360个上.

blocks.en:
The counterfactual data matters most.
With supervision on the decision of the expert only, the trajectories of two decisions end 2.65 m apart instead of 8.39 m, the trajectory follows every forced decision on 32.4% of the frames instead of 99.0%, and the collision rate under a label commitment rises from 0.50% to 1.08%.
Removing ℒ ground \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{ground}} and ℒ sem \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{sem}} leaves these measures almost unchanged, since ℒ exec \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{exec}} still supervises the generated trajectory and requires it to be read back as the decision.
The two losses supervise the code of the Maneuver Bank, which these measures do not capture.
Without them, the grounding head receives no supervision, and the nominal speed profile w ^ \hat{w} that it decodes from the code no longer matches the decision.
On the training frames, it deviates from the speed profile of its target by 4.77 m/s on average, compared with 0.22 m/s with the two losses.
Freezing the speed branch raises the collision rate under a label commitment from 0.50% to 0.60%.
blocks.zh:
反事实数据最为重要.
由于只监督专家的决定,两个决定的轨迹相距2.65米,而不是相距8.39米,轨迹沿循每个强制决定的32.4%的框架而不是99.0%的框架,标签承诺下的相撞率从0.50%上升到1.08%。

blocks.en: E.4 Decision Interventions
blocks.zh: E.4 决定干预

blocks.en:
Tab. A12 gives the follow rate of Eq. A12 for every decision.
A decision is evaluated on the frames on which an execution of it exists, between 2,509 and 3,429 of the 3,434 frames of the subset.
On the validation subset, the trajectory of MindDrive follows a forced speed token on 27% to 30% of the frames.
Its seven candidate trajectories fall into one decision on 86% of the frames, and the candidates of two speed tokens that name different decisions end only 0.51 m apart on average.
The token is an index without a kinematic meaning.
The trajectory of Commit2Drive follows a forced decision on at least 99% of the frames for each of the four decisions, and the trajectories of two decisions end 8.38 m apart on average, close to the 8.49 m of the executions that supervise them.
On the full validation set (10,806 labeled frames), the trajectory of MindDrive follows a forced speed token on 25% to 36% of the frames, and that of Commit2Drive again on at least 99%.

Forcing the commentary to a decision moves the trajectory into this decision on 32% of the frames on average, whereas an explicit instruction, the task that Action Dreaming trains, succeeds on 94% to 100%.
The trajectory therefore depends much less on the decision that the model itself states than on an external instruction.
The official agent of SimLingo keeps the dropout of its adapters active at inference, and we run the interventions with and without it.

blocks.en: E.5 Consistency across Scene Types
blocks.zh: E.5 场景类型的一致性

blocks.en:
Frames are assigned to scene types from the privileged simulator state and the scenario of the route.
Model outputs are not used, so the scene types are the same for all models.
A frame belongs to C1 if the route turns by more than 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} within the distance that the ego vehicle covers in 3 s, at least 15 m; C2 if a pedestrian or cyclist is within 20 m or inside the ego corridor; C3 if a vehicle has a time to collision below 3 s or cuts into the corridor; C4 if the ego vehicle is slower than 1 m/s, a red light or a stop sign of the ego lane is within 30 m, or a stationary vehicle blocks the corridor within 20 m; C5 if a static obstacle is inside the corridor; C6 at night or in rain;
and C7 if at least three moving agents are within 30 m and a vehicle is in the corridor.
A frame also belongs to C1, C2, C3, C5 or C7 if the scenario of its route is of this type.
A frame is simple if none of the conditions on the simulator state holds and the ego vehicle drives at more than 3 m/s, and complex if it belongs to at least one scene type and is not simple.

Tab. A13 gives the gaps and the infraction rate of each scene type.
For MindDrive and ORION, the say-exec gap grows from 13.2% and 9.1% on simple frames to 63.3% and 69.1% on complex ones.
It peaks at 82.2% and 87.8% on stopped or low-speed frames (C4), the scene type with the highest infraction rate.
SimLingo shows the opposite order for the say-exec gap, with 28.1% on simple frames and 15.8% on complex ones, while its say-do gap more than doubles.

blocks.en: E.6 Perception versus Language
blocks.zh: E.6 观念与语言

blocks.en:
Commit2Drive grounds the decision in facts that the perception of the model reports. Tab. A15 motivates this design with ORION [ 9 ] , whose language head can be asked about the facts that its perception heads report.
We compare two facts in closed loop, a hazard and a red light, and list the two conditions of the red light separately.
A hazard is reported when a vehicle or a vulnerable road user, rolled out at constant velocity, meets the front of the ego vehicle within 3 s.
A red light is reported when a traffic light governs the ego lane and is red.
Each disagreement is checked against the privileged simulator state with a tolerance band, and frames inside the band are not scored.
The answers of the language head contradict the perception of the model itself most often for the hazard, on 12.9% of the frames on which this fact is scored and 14.8% of the complex ones, and the language head is wrong in 84% of the scored disagreements.
On the open-loop validation frames, the same analysis gives a see-say gap of 0.4% on simple frames and 14.9% on complex ones on average over the facts, with the language head wrong in 94% of the scored disagreements.
Perception is the more reliable source for the hazard and as accurate as the language head for the red light, so Commit2Drive builds the admissible set at inference from the perception facts.

在开放校验框架上,同样的分析给出了简单框架上0.4%和复杂框架上平均14.9%的目测差距,94%的得分分歧中语言头有误.

blocks.en: E.7 Rule-Based Decisions
blocks.zh: E.7 根据规则作出的决定

blocks.en:
Tab. A15 lists the two rule-based functions of Sec. 4.4 .
A triggered rule issues the decision in place of the Decision Expert, and the Action Expert executes it without modification or retraining.
The experiment tests this extensibility, without evaluating the quality of the two rules.
On Dev10, the DS changes from 53.09 to 51.57 with the rules active.
In the Dev10 run that measures the latency of a rule-issued decision ( Sec. E.1 ), a rule issues the decision on 7,375 of the 26,209 steps (28.1%), and the trajectory of the Action Expert realizes the rule-issued decision on 7,372 of them.
Given the hidden state h a h_{a} , the Maneuver Bank and the speed branch take a median of 14.7 ms on one CPU thread for one commitment.
